findings.title: canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all-groups
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Holding only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource therefore makes `canManage()` true.

`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` gates on `auth.groups().requireManage()`. An admin who was only granted read access to groups can then:
- create new top-level groups, and
- move any existing group (by id) to the top level.

This is a privilege escalation. The check should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, matching `canManage(GroupModel)`.

The interface javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same wrong behavior and should be fixed too.

No test checks that a view-only all-groups permission cannot create groups; one should be added.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authz resource ID instead of the group ID
findings.body:
The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to `hasPermission(...)` and adds the same value to `granted`. V2 resources are named after the group ID, and `hasPermission` looks them up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Two things go wrong:
- The lookup by resource UUID always misses, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource and the group-specific permission is never evaluated.
- The returned set contains resource UUIDs, not group IDs.

The all-groups resource is the only one created with type `Groups` (`getOrCreateResource` never sets a type). So an admin with an all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members` permission gets a set holding just that resource's UUID.

`UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` put this set into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`, and `getUsersCount` passes it to the store. User search is then restricted to members of a non-existent group and returns nothing, and counts are wrong. The fix is to pass and collect `groupResource.getName()`, and to find per-group resources correctly. A test covering all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS with user search/count is missing.

findings.title: Group checks fail for realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change
findings.body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change therefore never get:
- the `Groups` all-resource, or
- the new `manage-membership`, `manage-members` and `view-members` scopes.

In such a realm, `getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` returns null. `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` then dereferences the null resource, so every group permission check for a non-role admin (listing groups, viewing a group, user search via `canViewByGroup`) can fail with a 500.

Creating a group permission also fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")`.

The code should guard against a null type resource, and `init` (or a migration) should add missing resource types and scopes to existing admin-permission clients.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. It actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, which checks the `manage-members` scope, not `manage-membership`. The text is a copy of the `requireManageMembership` doc and misdescribes which permission is enforced.
